title: Mods
summary: JayV has a mod system, like games do: every mod is a package with a version and an author that adds to the app through its extension points. Today they are LLM engines (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Kilo Code, OpenRouter, LiteLLM), agents (like Ollama and LM Studio) and optional features: statistics, gatehouse board, live files, chat search, project notes, second opinion, plan before building, parallel agents, earlier answers, lean code, symbol index, MCP, skills, skills.sh and find in conversation. One mod can bring several of them and need other mods. Every mod lives in the public repository jayv-coder-mods and reaches the app and the site as a catalog; the mods that came with the app install themselves, turned on, when you sign in.
usage: Open Settings › Mods. Under Installed, turn each mod on or off, open its settings or uninstall it; under Available in the catalog, Install adds a mod (and the mods it needs). Search filters both lists by name, description or author. The changes apply when you save, in this environment and on your other computers; the site (Dashboard › Mods) shows and changes the same mods. A mod that came installed does not come back on its own after you uninstall it. A mod that needs a newer JayV waits for the update. Your plan still decides: what it doesn't include stays off, and what it locks stays on. Also in the command palette (Ctrl+K): Install mod, Turn on mod, Turn off mod and Uninstall mod.
